title: Removal and Preservation of the Urinary Bladder
author: Firuoz Danashgeri
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8fahtie

steps.title: Anesthetize and Open Abdominal Wall
steps.instruction: Anesthetize or euthanize animals using approved methods and place them on their backs. Make a midline incision in the lower abdominal wall up to the pubic symphysis.

steps.title: Enter Abdominal Cavity
steps.instruction: Dissect through the muscle layer to enter the abdominal cavity, ensuring the muscle layer is tented up to prevent premature entry and injury to intraabdominal organs.

substeps.instruction: Lift the muscles of the abdominal wall with a pick up in the left hand.
Make an incision with scissors in the right hand.

steps.title: Isolate the Bladder
steps.instruction: Locate the bladder in the lower center of the abdomen near the pelvic bone and isolate it from surrounding structures.

substeps.instruction: Cut the median umbilical ligament connecting the ventral surface of the bladder to the abdominal wall.
Gently pull the bladder out of the abdomen using forceps on the dome to dissect it away from the vas deferens and seminal vesicles.
Clean fat and connective tissue surrounding the bladder and prostate caudally until the urethra is visible.

steps.title: Remove the Bladder
steps.instruction: Detach and remove the bladder from the abdominal cavity.

substeps.instruction: Cut the ureters as close to the bladder as possible.
Cut the urethra as far caudally as possible to remove the bladder.
Weight the bladder and immediately place it in physiological buffer (Krebs’ solution).

steps.title: Prepare Materials and Equilibrate Tissue
steps.instruction: Equilibrate the bladder in Krebs’ solution for at least 10 minutes and prepare the necessary containers.

substeps.instruction: Label two surgical pathology cassettes.
Prepare a secure container (centrifuge tube) with 40-50 ml Krebs’ solution at 4°C.
Label two micro centrifuge tubes.
Prepare a Crymold.
Ensure the bladder weight is recorded.

steps.title: Section the Bladder
steps.instruction: Using a sharp straight blade, section the bladder on a hard surface while soaked in Krebs’ solution.

substeps.instruction: Cut the bladder in half at its equatorial line.
Slice a full circumference section (minimum width 3 mm) from the upper (cephalad) half.

steps.title: Preserve Cephalad Tissue
steps.instruction: Preserve the cephalad portions of the bladder for contractility and subsequent processing.

substeps.instruction: Place the 3 mm slice into a tube containing 40-50 ml Krebs’ solution (4°C) for contractility studies (must arrive at lab within 24 hours).
Place the remaining cephalad portion in 4°C phosphate-buffered saline solution.

steps.title: Preserve Caudal Tissue
steps.instruction: Section and preserve the lower (caudal) half of the bladder for histology and immunohistochemistry.

substeps.instruction: Slice a full circumference section (minimum width 3 mm) from the lower half.
Place this section in 10% neutral buffered formalin (pH 7.0) in a surgical cassette at room temperature, preserving the circular orientation.
Place the remaining caudal portion upside down in a crymold to preserve anatomical orientation.
Bind and cover the tissue with OCT compound.
Snap-freeze the specimen in liquid nitrogen and store at –80ºC.

steps.title: Separate Urothelium from Muscle
steps.instruction: Separate the urothelium from the underlying detrusor muscle using a dissecting microscope or magnifying lens.

substeps.instruction: Pin the remaining bladder tissue at its four corners to a hard surface.
Lift the urothelium with microdissecting pick ups.
Insert microdissecting scissors into the plane between the two layers and open the jaws to expand the plane.
Repeat the process, cutting attachments as necessary, until the urothelium is separated from the muscle.

steps.title: Store Molecular Samples
steps.instruction: Preserve the separated layers for Western blotting and RT-PCR.

substeps.instruction: Place the urothelium and muscle into separate microcentrifuge tubes.
Freeze both samples in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C.
